attack_mechanism: Probing `aes_cipher_top.sa01_next` in this first-round window gives a chosen-plaintext attacker an exact intermediate against which candidate key bytes can be tested. Immediately after `ld_r` loads the state registers with `text_in_r XOR w[0:3]`, the combinational AES round network evaluates the first SubBytes/ShiftRows/MixColumns result. `aes_cipher_top.sa01_next` is the next-state byte at position (0,1), formed by XORing that transformed state with the matching expanded-key byte from `w[1]`. Signal propagation follows `aes_cipher_top.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.w[1] -> aes_cipher_top.u0.wo_1 -> aes_cipher_top.w1 -> aes_cipher_top.sa01_next`. The observation acts as a first-round oracle and can disclose the corresponding round-key, then master-key, bytes.

Sampling `aes_cipher_top.sa01_next` at fixed round offsets across repeated encryptions yields aligned nonlinear intermediates rather than only the final ciphertext. As `dcnt` advances the remaining rounds with `ld_r = 0`, the same combinational next-state node is reevaluated from the current state and current expanded key. `aes_cipher_top.sa01_next` exposes the pre-register value that will be captured into `sa01` at the next rising edge. Signal propagation follows `aes_cipher_top.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.w[1] -> aes_cipher_top.u0.wo_1 -> aes_cipher_top.w1 -> aes_cipher_top.sa01_next`. Those internal observations support differential or hypothesis-based recovery of round-key material that is invertible to the primary AES-128 key.

If the plaintext byte is known or chosen, reading `aes_cipher_top.sa31` allows the attacker to XOR away that plaintext and recover the corresponding master-key byte. One cycle after `ld`, `ld_r` selects the initial AddRoundKey arm for every AES state byte. `aes_cipher_top.sa31` contains the byte at state position (3,1) produced from a `text_in_r` byte XORed with the matching byte of `w[1]`. Signal propagation follows `aes_cipher_top.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.w[1] -> aes_cipher_top.u0.wo_1 -> aes_cipher_top.w1 -> aes_cipher_top.sa31`. The candidate therefore provides direct byte-wise key disclosure during cipher initialization.

Cycle-aligned observations of `aes_cipher_top.sa31` across chosen plaintexts reveal internal round states that can be related to the known AES transformations and candidate key hypotheses. After the initial load, `ld_r` is low and the same state location is updated from SubBytes/ShiftRows/MixColumns data XORed with the current expanded-key byte. `aes_cipher_top.sa31` carries this key-dependent intermediate on each active encryption round. Signal propagation follows `aes_cipher_top.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.key -> aes_cipher_top.u0.w[1] -> aes_cipher_top.u0.wo_1 -> aes_cipher_top.w1 -> aes_cipher_top.sa31`.
